rationale: The validation report explicitly flags issue == 'vulnerable_accepted': the differential run shows the shipped insecure baseline (which re-reads desc->length in the copy loop 'for (uint32_t i = 0; i < desc->length; i++)' and in the return statement 'return static_cast<int>(desc->length)') passes SR1 and SR2 identically to the golden solution. Both golden_run and vulnerable_run produce the exact same stdout ('[TEST] PASS' for every requirement including SR1 and SR2), so the TOCTOU mutation/race harness in evaluation/harness_main.cpp and evaluate.py fails to discriminate between the hardened and vulnerable implementations. This is a core evaluation_framework defect, not a specification or artifact problem: the golden solution is behaviorally correct (single snapshot read), the baseline is genuinely vulnerable (double-fetch of desc->length), but the harness's concurrent-mutation mechanism does not reliably force the race window, so it never observes the vulnerable code using a post-mutation length. mutation_score=0.0 is not meaningful here per the mutation_score_meaningful=false flag and mutation_status='blocked_by_differential' — the preflight differential check must pass before mutation testing is valid. requirement_discrimination_coverage_score=0.0 confirms none of the SR checks discriminate in practice despite requirement_mapping_coverage_score=1.0 on paper. Per the vulnerable_accepted rule, this must route to evaluation_framework for repair.
revision_instructions: evaluate.py / evaluation/harness_main.cpp currently accepts the shipped insecure baseline on SR1 and SR2 (differential.vulnerable_run.status='pass' but expected 'fail'). The baseline vulnerability is a double-fetch: it reads the shared volatile length field once for validation, then reads it again both in the copy-loop bound and in the return statement, creating a time-of-check-to-time-of-use window. The current sustained-overwrite/background-mutator-thread approach to force a race between the validating read and the later read is not reliably triggering the vulnerable path even though -O0 is used; redesign the detection mechanism to be deterministic rather than a best-effort race. Concretely: wrap the shared length field access behind an instrumented accessor (a function or object with a read-side-effect) that the test harness controls, so the harness can pause execution deterministically between the first read (used for validation) and any subsequent read of the same field, then mutate the underlying value during that pause before allowing execution to continue. The check must FAIL if it observes more than one read of the field per invocation, or if the transferred byte count, return value, or destination buffer contents reflect the post-pause mutated value rather than the value observed at the first read. This must be a purely behavioral check driven through the pinned extern "C" run_transfer entry point — compile and execute the submission, do not pattern-match source text, since a correct rewrite may restructure the code differently from the golden while still reading the field exactly once. Before shipping, add a hard preflight/CI gate that runs the differential test (golden vs shipped baseline) and blocks publication unless golden_run.status=='pass' and vulnerable_run.status=='fail' for every SR requirement, especially SR1 and SR2. Also verify SR3's existing non-racy rejection-path check remains correct since it already passes on both runs.WordPress
